title: Configuration-aware tracer and collective lithium transport in exact-composition Li6.5La3Zr1.5Ta0.5O12
research_question: How much do crystallographic occupancy realization, velocity initialization, cell representation, and thermal volume alter tracer and collective Li transport predicted for experimentally matched LLZTO?
primary_estimands: collective charge diffusivity and activation energy
room-temperature extrapolation versus exact-composition NMR and impedance benchmarks
stopping_rule: A temperature point is usable only when tracer and, separately, collective MSD have a 0.8-1.2 log-log exponent, at least 20 A^2 displacement at the maximum analyzed lag, at least four valid non-overlapping blocks, and relative block standard error no larger than 0.5. Unresolved points are reported and rerun under a longer, newly fingerprinted protocol; they are never dropped from an Arrhenius series.

gates.criterion: Full test suite, compilation, package lock, pinned input hashes, model-weight hash, and clean diff checks pass before new production data are accepted.

At 800 K, 1 fs and 2 fs NVE pilots remain structurally stable; the selected step has absolute total-energy drift no larger than 1 meV atom-1 ps-1, and transport estimates are compared without treating a short pilot as converged.

Representative relaxed and finite-temperature snapshots must be checked against a consistent DFT reference set. Target errors are documented before looking at transport agreement; failure blocks publication claims from the universal potential.
Every Arrhenius temperature independently passes the preregistered tracer and collective adequacy checks. Literature precedent uses 0.5 ns over 700-900 K; shorter runs are pilots only.
Report between-occupancy and velocity-seed variation, and compare the 94-atom primitive realization with the 188-atom conventional cubic realization at 800 K.

Compare NMR tracer diffusion only with tracer predictions and impedance conductivity only with collective predictions; retain phase, density, sample type, temperature extrapolation, and DOI provenance.
